title: The Cat and the Crow

full_text:
In an orchard of fig trees lived a quiet tabby cat and a noisy, conceited crow who nested in the tallest poplar. The crow spent his days strutting upon the branches, cawing loudly to the sky, boasting of his glossy black feathers, his sharp beak, and his ancient lineage.

Whenever the cat crept softly through the grass to catch grasshoppers, the crow would mock her: 'Look at you, poor four-legged creature! You have to slink through the dust on belly and paws, while I command the winds and fill the valley with my royal song!' The cat flicked her ears, kept her counsel, and said nothing.

One morning, a fowler entered the orchard carrying a hunting bow and sticky lime-twigs. The cat, sensing danger with her acute instincts, slipped silently beneath the dense thorns of a blackberry bramble, keeping her tail tucked and her body motionless, blending completely with the dark earth.

The crow, by contrast, remained upon his high perch, flapped his wings, and began cawing with deafening pride, believing that his loud voice would intimidate the intruder. 'Hear my battle-cry, human!' cawed the crow. 'None dare disturb my orchard!'

The fowler looked up, guided directly by the bird’s ceaseless noise. He fitted a slender reed arrow to his bow, drew the string to his ear, and loosed the shaft. The arrow struck the crow in the wing, sending him fluttering and tumbling from his high branch down into the blackberry bush.

The cat stepped out quietly from her thorny refuge, looked at the wounded, trembling crow, and said gently: 'Brother, the hunter did not possess magic eyes; your own tongue was the compass that guided his arrow to your heart. Had you possessed the wisdom to keep silent in times of peril, your feathers would still be dry in the tree.' The cat helped the humbled crow into a safe hollow in the roots, teaching him that quiet humility is a fortress that pride can never build.
moral: Quiet discretion and humility provide safety, while noisy vanity attracts the hunter's eye.
